The instant application has been moved by the applicants namely Vinod Kumar Mishra, Smt. Learned counsel for the parties submitted that the parties have amicably settled the dispute which was private in nature and has submitted a compromise deed before this Court, which under the orders of this Court was sent to the trial Court for verification and the parties after appearing before the trial Court had accepted the terms of the compromise deed and the trial Court has also verified the same and the report of the trial court as well as the copy of the compromise has been brought on record by supplementary affidavit dated 29.08.2022.
It is further submitted that the other disputes between the parties pending at the level of National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench has also been settled and,
thus, the proceedings of the instant case be also quashed in the light of the compromise arrived at between the parties.
Learned A.G.A. would have no objection to the request made by learned counsel for the parties as the dispute between the parties is purely of personal in nature.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that the dispute between the parties was purely of personal in nature.

4.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has stated that by means of aforesaid order dated 16.11.2022,
the entire proceedings pursuant to the FIR No.507 of 2017 have been quashed by this Court.

5. The impugned FIR is an offshoot of Case Crime No.507 of 2017 for the reason that despite the process being issued by the court concerned, the petitioners have not appeared before the court concerned.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has further submitted that when the FIR bearing No.507 of 2017 and its consequential criminal proceedings have been quashed, the impugned FIR and its consequential criminal proceedings may be quashed.

6. Sri Aniruddh Kumar Singh, learned AGA-I, has however stated that in the FIR No.507 of 2017,
the allegations are different whereas the impugned FIR has been registered under Section 174-A of IPC for the reason that the petitioners have ignored the process being issued by the court, therefore,
they have been declared proclaimed offender.
However, he has submitted that there is no dispute that the impugned FIR under Section 174-A of IPC is an offshoot of FIR No.507 of 2017.

7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case and the arguments so advanced by the learned counsel for the parties as well as the order dated 16.11.2022 (supra) and the judgments of the Apex Court cited in the order dated 16.11.2022 (supra), I find that this petition deserves to be allowed.

Thus, the entire proceedings of Criminal Case No.43930 of 2018 (supra) arising out of FIR No.212 of 2018, under Section 174-A of IPC, Police Station- Krishna Nagar, District- Lucknow are hereby quashed in respect of the present petitioners.
8. Accordingly, the instant petition is allowed.
